newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends weaker at 492.50/493.50/dlr.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends weaker at 492.50/493.50/dlr.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed weaker at 492.50/493.50 per dollar Thursday as the Central Bank sold dollars heavily to prevent a steeper slide of the local currency, traders said.
The bolivar closed at 492.00/493.00 Wednesday and has slipped 4.25 bolivars per dollar so far this week.
"The market was heavily demanded, particularly on the corporate side and the dollar reached 494.50 bolivars. But the Central Bank came in strongly and brought it down," one trader said.
Traders said the heavy dollar demand was due largely to excess liquidity on money markets, echoing comments made by Central Bank President Antonio Casas Gonzalez earlier in the day.
They added that the Central Bank's strong dollar selling in the afternoon should calm market expectations that it was prepared to allow the bolivar to plummet further.

Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars, which blurs the difference between the Central Bank supplying liquidity and intervening.
Venezuela continues to pursue an inflation-fighting strong bolivar policy, where the currency ostensibly floats between slowly depreciating bands set by Central Bank intervention.
Critics say the policy has left the bolivar increasingly over-valued with the exchange rate little-changed since price and currency controls were removed in April last year.
